# VibePascal v58 -- cross-platform status manifest
# Cut by FPCDeveloper (Otto).  win64 + linux64 shipped 2026-09-11 (cy1117);
# i386-linux-cross, arm-linux-cross, aarch64-linux and arm-linux shipped
# 2026-09-11 (cy1118); x86_64-darwin and aarch64-darwin shipped 2026-09-11
# (cy1119).  v58 is now on EVERY target this fork publishes.  The section at
# the end records that the macOS pair shipped hours after the rest, and why,
# rather than quietly erasing the gap.
# This file is the authoritative answer to "which platforms have v58".
# Per-platform detail lives in dist/<target>/VERSION.txt and inside each tarball.
# There is no RELEASE-v57.txt: v57 shipped to win64 and linux64 only, and every
# target that skipped it collects it here, so v57 is documented below too.

source_commit: dedf242c696a543f9626e2839ced40876478a98a
compiler_fix:  dedf242c69  (compiler/entfile.pas -- tppufile.readheader)
parent:        v57 (1f605f41b3b06a5fa84fb4cb31ee4298fb30907f, fix c31227c8ca)

WHAT CHANGED IN v57 AND v58 -- ONE ACCIDENT, TWO BYTES APART
  Both fixes are about the same thing happening to a unit file: a killed build,
  a full disk or an interrupted copy leaves a .ppu HALF WRITTEN.

  v57 (c31227c8ca)  A short read inside the .ppu reader is now an error.  Before
                    it, a half-written unit could put the compiler into an
                    infinite 99%-CPU spin with no message at all -- you had to
                    notice a build that never ended and go looking.

  v58 (dedf242c69)  v57 only ever noticed damage it happened to trip over.  Lose
                    the TAIL of a unit and there is nothing to trip over, because
                    nothing an interface load reads lives in the last handful of
                    bytes: the compiler read what it wanted, never reached the
                    missing part, and built your program against a unit that is
                    not all there.  Exit 0, no message, nothing to search a log
                    for.  Measured on a real 55291-byte unit, every truncation
                    from 55271 bytes upward was accepted.
                    A .ppu header records how long the payload is, so a complete
                    file is always 40 bytes of header plus that number and can
                    never be fewer.  tppufile.readheader now compares the two and
                    rejects a SHORT file.  Longer than declared stays legal, as
                    it always was.  The arithmetic is 64-bit on purpose: the
                    declared size is an unsigned 32-bit field, and a corrupt
                    header claiming near 4 GB would wrap a 32-bit sum and switch
                    the check off at exactly the moment it is needed.

  THIS DOES NOT TURN GOOD BUILDS RED.  The rejection is soft and self-healing: a
  truncated unit whose source is available is RECOMPILED and the build goes
  green; a good copy of the same unit in a later -Fu directory is used instead;
  only a truncated unit with no source and no other copy stops the compile, and
  it stops with the message an absent unit already gives.  Nobody is ever told to
  go and delete a file.

  COMPILER-BINARY-ONLY.  No PPU FORMAT change -- the reader got stricter, the
  format did not move -- and no RTL or package change, so existing unit sets stay
  valid on every platform.

IN-TREE CROSS COMPILERS THE SAME REBUILD TOUCHED -- NOT PUBLISHED, BUT DEPENDED ON
  These live only in the working tree. They have no tarball and no download, so
  they are not "platforms" above. They are listed because at least one of them is
  exec'd by a downstream gate -- compiler/ppcrossaarch64 is a SYMLINK to
  compiler/ppcrossa64, and BuildMaster's aarch64-linux Lazarus roll and loadcheck
  run through that symlink. A binary something depends on should not be the one
  the manifest is silent about.

    compiler/ppcrossa64   md5 eab972e2457f458e0c42bd2a51afa4d6  (= ppcrossaarch64)
                          carries v58. Measured, not inferred from its mtime:
                          dist/ppu-truncation-check.sh ... aarch64-linux scores
                          25/25 clean rc=0, and the preserved predecessor
                          (md5 877b3046..) scores 11/25 rc=1 on the same command.
                          Measured independently by BuildMaster and again here
                          against aarch64-darwin .ppu files, same 25/25.
    compiler/ppcross386   md5 b76969a5226f68019f287a97dac89333
    compiler/ppcrossarm   md5 5e3d9ba2d978db06b31a1a15c37244d9
                          -- these two DO have published artifacts, listed above
                             under i386-linux-cross/ and arm-linux-cross/.

  A fresh md5 alone would not have established any of this: an incremental build
  that recompiled one file emits one too. See the unit-count section below.

HOW EACH BINARY WAS SHOWN TO CARRY THE FIX -- AND WHY NOT BY VERSION STRING
  Every one of these compilers reports "3.3.1".  The version string cannot tell
  v54 from v58, so it was never used as evidence.  The discriminating test is
  dist/ppu-truncation-check.sh: truncate a REAL .ppu for that target at 25
  offsets and score what the compiler does, with the unit in exactly ONE
  directory and its source off every search path -- otherwise a correct rejection
  resolves from a shadow copy and reads as a pass.

  Each new binary was run against the PRESERVED binary it replaces, the one that
  actually shipped, re-run this cycle rather than argued from source:

    target             replaced binary        pre-fix           post-fix
    i386-linux         ppcross386  v54        11/25, exit 1     25/25, exit 0
    arm-linux (cross)  ppcrossarm  v54        11/25, exit 1     25/25, exit 0
    aarch64-linux      ppca64      v56        11/25, exit 1     25/25, exit 0
    arm-linux (native) ppcarm      v56        12/25, exit 1     25/25, exit 0
    x86_64-darwin      ppcx64      v56        11/25, exit 1     25/25, exit 0
    aarch64-darwin     ppca64      v56        11/25, exit 1     25/25, exit 0

  THE TWO DARWIN ROWS ARE NOT THE SHIPPED MACH-O BINARIES, and saying so is the
  point.  Nothing here can execute a Mach-O, so those two lines were measured on
  Linux-hosted compilers built from the SAME source commit, targeting darwin and
  reading real <arch>-darwin .ppu files.  They are evidence about the SOURCE the
  shipped binaries were built from, not about the shipped binaries running.  What
  ties the source to the bytes is the section triage in the darwin VERSION.txt
  files: v56 source vs v58 source, both cross-built here today with the same host
  compiler, RTL and flags, __text +896 (x86_64) and +784 (aarch64), against a
  build-noise floor of SEVENTEEN BYTES of LC_UUID on the Intel side and identical
  section sizes on the arm64 side.

  The pre-fix failures split into a loud half and a silent half: 8 or 9 offsets
  HUNG and had to be killed at 30 seconds, and 5 were ACCEPTED with rc=0 -- a
  corrupt unit taken as valid, which is the half v58 exists for.  The native arm
  compiler scores 13 problems where its cross twin scores 14; one offset that
  spins on the host binary errors out on the native one.  That is reported as
  measured rather than rounded to match, and the silent five are identical on
  every target.

A CROSS BUILD CAN LIE ABOUT BEING ONE -- CHECK THE UNIT COUNT, NOT THE HASH
  Recorded because it nearly shipped four stale compilers with fresh hashes.
  The first ppcross386 build this cycle compiled ONE file (pp.pas, 795 lines),
  never touched the patched entfile.pas, reused units from 2026-09-03 for
  everything else -- and emitted a NEW md5, which reads exactly like a successful
  rebuild.  A separate incremental arm build did worse: it crashed the driver
  compiler with an access violation.  Both were cured by wiping
  compiler/<target>/{bin,units} and rebuilding from scratch, with no source
  change.  Units recompiled per binary this release: 277 (i386), 223 (aarch64),
  241 (arm), 250 (x86_64-darwin), 223 (aarch64-darwin).  If you
  reproduce these, assert that count.

ADDENDUM 2026-09-11 (cy1119): THE MACOS PAIR SHIPPED, HOURS AFTER THE REST
  Both darwin targets now carry v58 and are listed above.  The paragraph below is
  left exactly as it was written earlier today, because it is the record of what
  this manifest said while the gap was open -- not because it is still true.  The
  one line in it that is now WRONG is "STILL ON v56"; everything it says about
  WHY the darwin delivery path is different is still correct and is why those two
  entries carry an extra SIGNING note and no runtime claim.

  Still true after this addendum, and the reason the honesty section above is
  worded the way it is: v58 is on every target, but the macOS pair is the only
  one where nobody has ever executed the shipped binary.

--- SUPERSEDED, KEPT VERBATIM (written 2026-09-11, cy1118) ---
STILL ON v56 AFTER THIS RELEASE
  x86_64-darwin/   vibepascal-v56-a187bbac34-x86_64-darwin-bin.tar.gz
  aarch64-darwin/  vibepascal-v56-a187bbac34-aarch64-darwin-bin.tar.gz

  Both macOS targets are missing v57 AND v58.  On those compilers a half-written
  unit still hangs forever and a tail-truncated one is still taken as valid.
  Nobody is blocked on anybody: it is a build step, and darwin is NOT blocked on
  a missing SDK (pass -XR to mac_sdk/MacOSX26.2.sdk and both darwin targets
  link).  It is deliberately NOT bundled into this release because the darwin
  delivery path is different: build-release.sh ad-hoc signs every bundled Mach-O
  with rcodesign, a signature APPENDS bytes and CHANGES the hash, so publishing
  an unsigned staging hash there is the exact thing that reads to a careful user
  as corruption.  See the signing sections of dist/RELEASE-v56.txt before
  attempting it.  Tracked on the open ledger row darwin_stale_v58.

  Do not read this manifest as "the fix is everywhere".  It is on every Linux and
  Windows target and on neither macOS target.

--- ADDENDUM 2026-09-11 (cy1122): aarch64-linux NOW HAS A UNIT SET ---
Nothing above is retracted; this adds an artifact the manifest could not name
because it did not exist when the manifest was written.

  dist/aarch64-linux/vibepascal-v52-aarch64-linux-units.tar.gz
    84809752 bytes   md5 a8e82e441275abb2bc75a1554f2d7c56
    sha256 958db18cafa1c1d1677f1986bef73888672ae31961afea699ded783e2356da83
    1631 .ppu + 1584 .o, flat in units/aarch64-linux/

WHY THIS MATTERED MORE THAN A MISSING CONVENIENCE FILE.  Four aarch64-linux
releases (v54, v55, v56, v58) shipped a compiler binary and NO unit set, and this
target has never published one -- so on a box with no prior VibePascal install the
published bytes could not compile one line.  That violates our own rule that a
platform which has never shipped cannot go out bin-only, and it was found while
pinning bytes for a verification ask to the one native ARM64 host we have
(gx10-f8f9), where the honest answer to "can a user get from extract to a working
build" was no.  PACKAGING, NOT A BUILD: the PPUs already existed on disk and
nothing was compiled to produce this.

VERIFIED 2026-09-11 on these exact bytes: 144/144 packages load clean exit 0 with
zero recompiles; all 3215 tarball files byte-identical to the units that load
check measured; and extract-to-running-program from the published bytes only --
bin tarball plus this units tarball into an empty directory, a SysUtils/Classes
program compiled with -n (rc=0, ELF aarch64 static) and RUN (rc=0, correct
output), with the negative control firing when units/ is hidden (rc=1, "Can't
find unit system").  Under qemu-aarch64-static, which is not silicon.  Details
and the exact commands in dist/aarch64-linux/UNITS.txt.

v52 UNITS WITH A v58 COMPILER IS NOMINAL ONLY HERE, AND IT IS MEASURED:
"git diff --stat 34660520 HEAD -- rtl/ packages/" is EMPTY.  RTL and package
source did not move between v52 and v58 -- only compiler/ did (10 files, 407
insertions) -- and the PPU format did not move either (v208 / LongVersion 30).
A v58-stamped rebuild would compile the same source these were compiled from.

dist/aarch64-linux/VERSION.txt IS DELIBERATELY UNTOUCHED.  It is byte-identical
(md5 1b1c71191ddefdc461cec628f0cdcf03) to the copy inside the published v58 bin
tarball, and rewriting it would make the repo and the shipped artifact disagree.
The pairing requirement therefore lives in the new, mirrored-nowhere
dist/aarch64-linux/UNITS.txt.

STILL OPEN AFTER THIS, so the gap is not mis-reported as closed: five other
targets publish a compiler binary and no unit set (arm-linux-cross,
i386-linux-cross, linux64, x86_64-darwin, aarch64-darwin), and the arm-linux v54
units tarball is RTL-ONLY (99 .ppu) where win64 and now aarch64-linux ship the
full RTL+packages set.  Whether each of those gaps BITES depends on whether units
reach that target's users by another route, which is being measured per target
rather than answered by counting tarballs.


ADDENDUM 2026-09-11 (cy1123) -- arm-linux GOES FROM RTL-ONLY TO A FULL UNIT SET
===============================================================================
The paragraph immediately above names arm-linux as a remaining gap.  That half is
now closed, in the same PACKAGING-not-a-build shape as the aarch64 one: the
package PPUs already existed and were already verified, they had simply never
been cut into a tarball.  Policy #13 safe -- nothing was compiled.

NEW:  dist/arm-linux/vibepascal-v54-arm-linux-units-full.tar.gz
      82757332 bytes
      md5    6e92ffab6cb292c65dc0dc393a487164
      sha256 aca16ac314da1730e3253c71807d2a8249fc4e31c5f54f98a5a2438afa855030
      3496 files flat in units/arm-linux/: 1646 .ppu (99 RTL + 1547 package),
      1600 .o, 249 .rsj, 1 .inc.
NEW:  dist/arm-linux/UNITS.txt (mirrored nowhere, so it can be corrected later).

THE OLD RTL-ONLY TARBALL IS KEPT, BYTE-UNTOUCHED, UNDER ITS OWN NAME.
vibepascal-v54-arm-linux-units.tar.gz (3353006 bytes, md5
bd4fa9afca17ed8d4595ddb1cafb9960) has been downloadable since 2026-09-10, so
anyone verifying it against its recorded hash must still succeed.  Replacing its
bytes under the same name would be indistinguishable from corruption on their
end.  It is a PROVEN strict subset: all 204 of its members were md5-compared
against the same-named members of the full set, 0 differences.

WHAT THE GAP ACTUALLY WAS, MEASURED ON A SINGLE AXIS.  Same compiler, same
command, same source, only the unit set differs:
    uses SysUtils, Classes;   old set rc=0    full set rc=0
    uses SysUtils, fpjson;    old set rc=1    full set rc=0
             ("pkgtest.pas(3,16) Fatal: Can't find unit fpjson used by pkgtest")

VERIFIED 2026-09-11 on these exact bytes, and the chain is the point rather than
any one number: 143/143 packages load clean exit 0 with zero recompiles
(dist/unit-set-loadcheck.sh arm-linux, compiler ppcrossarm); all 3496 tarball
files byte-identical by md5 to the tree units that load check measured, 0
mismatches; and extract-to-running-program from the published bytes only -- the
v58 bin tarball plus this units tarball into an empty directory, a program using
SysUtils + Classes + fpjson compiled with -n so this host's installed FPC could
supply nothing (rc=0, "ELF 32-bit LSB executable, ARM, EABI5, statically
linked"), RUN with correct output (NativeInt = 4).  NEGATIVE CONTROL FIRED:
identical command with units/ renamed away -> rc=1, "Can't find unit system used
by hello".  Under qemu-arm-static with arm-linux-gnueabihf cross binutils, which
is not a Raspberry Pi.

dist/arm-runtime-proof.sh NOW FOLLOWS THE ARTIFACT.  It named the RTL-only
tarball literally, so it would have gone on measuring the superseded bytes
forever; it now picks the units tarball the same highest-vN way it already picked
the bin tarball, preferring a "-full" set.  Re-run end to end after the change:
PASS, exit 0, every assertion identical, only the "using" line different.

dist/arm-linux/VERSION.txt IS DELIBERATELY UNTOUCHED.  It is byte-identical (md5
01e0ba5003dc90ccff0e12e6a63a46e1) to the copy inside the published v58 bin
tarball, and it names the OLD units tarball.  That line is incomplete rather than
wrong, and correcting it in place would make the repo and a shipped artifact
disagree -- so the correction lives in UNITS.txt instead.

v54 UNITS WITH A v58 COMPILER IS NOMINAL ONLY HERE TOO, AND IT IS MEASURED:
"git diff --stat b7d2d9676e HEAD -- rtl/ packages/" is EMPTY.  RTL and package
source did not move between v54 and v58; only compiler/ did (8 files, 210
insertions).

STILL OPEN AFTER THIS: i386-linux-cross publishes nothing at all for units (there
is no dist/i386-linux directory), and linux64, x86_64-darwin and aarch64-darwin
publish a compiler with no unit set.  None of those three has a BLOCKED consumer
today -- the fleet builds RTL+packages from the checkout for linux64, and the
Lazarus darwin tarball bundles a full 6754-unit darwin set -- which is why only
the two ARM targets have been cut.  This is not a plan to cut five tarballs on
principle.

NOBODY HAS STILL EVER RUN A VibePascal BINARY ON PHYSICAL ARM HARDWARE, 32-BIT OR
64-BIT.  That sentence has not changed and is not changed by this addendum.

ADDENDUM 2026-09-11 (later, cy1124) -- THE TWO CROSS TARGETS NOW HAVE UNITS TOO
================================================================================
The previous addendum closed arm-linux and ended with "STILL OPEN: i386-linux-cross
publishes nothing at all for units".  That is closed now, and arm-linux-cross --
which needed no new bytes -- has a pointer.  Both are PACKAGING, not builds: the
PPUs already existed and nothing was compiled (Policy #13).

NEW ARTIFACT
  dist/i386-linux-cross/vibepascal-v54-i386-linux-units-full.tar.gz
      84260313 bytes  md5 3e9ce41ec5a263d500ae5218c62d8280
      sha256 36a5a85feee223e39498a45b1398b149fe0911385e7ffe86af4117e6616f40b3
      3607 files: 1704 .ppu (108 RTL + 1596 package), 1652 .o, 250 .rsj, 1 .inc
  This is the FIRST units tarball this target has ever had, so nothing is
  superseded and no previously published hash changes.  Four compiler binaries
  had shipped for i386 with no unit set at all, which means the published bytes
  could not compile one line on a machine with no prior install.
  Full writeup: dist/i386-linux-cross/UNITS.txt.

NEW POINTER, NO NEW BYTES
  dist/arm-linux-cross/UNITS.txt.  The arm CROSS compiler targets arm-linux, so
  it consumes the SAME unit set as the native arm compiler -- an 82 MB tarball
  copied into a second directory would have been waste.  The file is a pointer
  to dist/arm-linux/vibepascal-v54-arm-linux-units-full.tar.gz.

AND THE REASON THAT POINTER IS NOT A ONE-LINER.  Running it before writing it
found something a user would have read as a broken unit set.  The arm cross
compiler is an x86_64 binary and left to itself calls the HOST linker:

    /usr/bin/ld.bfd: skipping incompatible ./units/arm-linux/varutils.o
    pkgtest.pas(18,1) Error: Error while linking                        rc=1

The units are fine; the LINKER is the wrong architecture.  Fix is
-XParm-linux-gnueabihf- plus binutils-arm-linux-gnueabihf, and the internal
linker is NOT a substitute (-Xi was tried and fell through to the same ld).
The i386 cross compiler is the OPPOSITE case and that contrast is now documented
on both files: stock x86_64 binutils already links elf_i386, so it needs no -XP
and no extra packages.

BOTH PROVEN EXTRACT-TO-RUNNING-PROGRAM FROM PUBLISHED BYTES, IN EMPTY DIRS, WITH
A PACKAGE UNIT (uses SysUtils, Classes, fpjson -- an RTL-only set passes a
hello-world and fails this, which is exactly how the arm gap stayed invisible):
  arm-linux-cross   rc=0, ELF 32-bit ARM EABI5 statically linked, RAN under
                    qemu-arm-static: HELLO vibepascal arm-linux-cross 2 {...}
  i386-linux-cross  rc=0, ELF 32-bit Intel 80386 statically linked, RAN
                    natively: HELLO vibepascal i386-linux 2 {...}
NEGATIVE CONTROLS FIRED AND WERE SCORED ON THEIR TEXT, NOT THEIR EXIT CODE --
"Can't find unit system used by hello" on both, plus an RTL-only-vs-full A/B on
i386 ("Can't find unit fpjson used by pkgonly").  An rc is not a reason: a
rejected flag returns rc=1 too, so a control can go void and still read as
firing.

PUBLISHED-VS-LOCAL WITHOUT AN 82 MB DOWNLOAD.  The arm units tarball was settled
with the GitHub contents API blob sha1 (7cdc30407935dbad3fcc63dd5e4c9eaefc4ae2c8
== local `git hash-object`, size 82757332 both sides) instead of a re-fetch.  The
two small compiler tarballs WERE re-downloaded unauthenticated and re-hashed.

NEITHER VERSION.txt WAS TOUCHED.  dist/arm-linux-cross/VERSION.txt (md5
18d45fee3024bdf4a9d731e604f21897) and dist/i386-linux-cross/VERSION.txt (md5
455282186da36bb2f505b70a0f055b1b) are byte-identical to the copies inside their
published bin tarballs, so the corrections live in UNITS.txt instead.

STILL OPEN AFTER THIS: linux64, x86_64-darwin and aarch64-darwin publish a
compiler with no unit set.  None has a blocked consumer today -- the fleet builds
RTL+packages from the checkout for linux64, and the Lazarus darwin tarball
bundles a full 6754-unit darwin set -- so they stay uncut until one turns up.
This is still not a plan to cut tarballs on principle.

NOBODY HAS STILL EVER RUN A VibePascal BINARY ON PHYSICAL ARM HARDWARE, AND
NOTHING HERE HAS RUN ON A REAL 32-BIT i386 USERLAND.  qemu-arm-static is an
emulator and x86_64 running i386 code is not a 32-bit install.


ADDENDUM 2026-09-11 (cycle 1126) -- THE ARM GATE PRINTED PASS OVER AN RTL-ONLY
UNIT SET, AND ITS aarch64 HALF HAD NEVER TOUCHED THE PUBLISHED UNITS AT ALL
==============================================================================
No bytes shipped here moved.  Only dist/arm-runtime-proof.sh,
dist/win64-runtime-proof.sh and two UNITS.txt files changed, and every claim
below was measured against a control tree of real directories (NOT symlinks --
find -maxdepth 1 -type f does not descend one, and a rig that sees nothing
reports the same failure as an artifact that is broken).  The unmodified tree
was run FIRST and passed, so each injected failure below is the defect and not
the rig.

THREE DEFECTS, ALL MEASURED, ALL IN GATES I HAD ALREADY CALLED GOOD:

1. AN RTL-ONLY UNIT SET PASSED.  With dist/arm-linux's -full tarball moved aside
   so the resolver fell back to the 206-member RTL-only set (fpjson absent),
   arm-runtime-proof.sh printed "ARM RUNTIME PROOF: PASS" and exited 0 -- every
   test it ran (tinlinevar*, tblockscopefinal1) resolves inside the RTL.  This is
   the exact hole that hid the RTL-only arm tarball for a day in cycle 1123, and
   it was still open in the gate that is supposed to catch it.  Both halves now
   compile and RUN a program that uses fpjson, a PACKAGE unit, and the same
   substitution now fails with
       pkgtest.pas(3,25) Fatal: Can't find unit fpjson used by pkgtest

2. THE aarch64 HALF MEASURED THE CHECKOUT, NOT THE RELEASE.  It compiled against
   $VP/rtl/units/aarch64-linux -- the tree -- which is RTL-only and predates the
   aarch64 units tarball existing (first published one cycle ago).  So the
   published aarch64 unit set had never been exercised by any committed gate.
   Same shape as defect 1: the tree was complete, the tarball was not, and only
   the tree was being measured.  It now extracts and uses the published set
   (resolved newest-first, never named literally).

3. A REFUSAL THAT BLAMED THE ARTIFACT FOR A BROKEN TREE.  With no arm bin
   tarball present the script printed "  using " and then
       tar (child): : Cannot open: No such file or directory
   at rc=2 -- which reads as a corrupt or truncated download, and rc=2 is also
   this script's "you have no qemu" code, so even the number was ambiguous.  The
   same hole was in win64-runtime-proof.sh in a different shape: every path there
   is read out of LATEST.txt, and deleting one line made tar report
       .../dist/win64/: Cannot read: Is a directory
       gzip: stdin: unexpected end of file
   i.e. archive corruption, from a missing line in a text file.  Both now name
   what they looked for, where, and say NOTHING WAS TESTED, at rc=1.  Measured
   A/B: pre-patch rc=2 with the tar spew, post-patch rc=1 with the named cause.

WHY THESE THREE AND NOT A SWEEP: BuildMaster reproduced dist/cross-runtime-proof.sh
independently this cycle and reported that two of his OWN control rigs were broken
(symlinked dist dirs; then cp -al across a filesystem boundary) and that both
exited with the SAME code as the defect he had injected -- only the message TEXT
separated them.  That is the generalisation: a gate whose refusals name their own
cause can tell a user "your rig is broken" apart from "your artifact is broken".
These were my gates that could not.

ALSO: arm-runtime-proof.sh's workdir default moved from /tmp (a 2 GB tmpfs shared
with every other agent on this host) to $HOME/.cache/vp-arm-proof, after the first
run carrying both unit sets died mid-extract with "Cannot write: No space left on
device".  Both sibling gates had already moved off tmpfs.  A complete run leaves
807 MB (measured); under 2 GB free is now refused UP FRONT, named, at rc=2.

VERIFIED AFTER THE CHANGE: both scripts re-run end to end on the real tree --
arm-runtime-proof.sh PASS rc=0 (now including "pkgtest (uses fpjson, a PACKAGE
unit) compiled and ran" on ARM and on aarch64, NativeInt 4 and 8), and
win64-runtime-proof.sh ALL STAGES PASSED rc=0 under wine64 with its pre-fix
controls still firing.  No tarball, binary or VERSION.txt was touched.

STILL TRUE, UNCHANGED BY ANY OF THIS: every ARM result above is qemu-user on an
x86_64 host.  NOBODY HAS EVER RUN A VibePascal BINARY ON PHYSICAL ARM SILICON,
ON A MAC, OR ON REAL WINDOWS.
